story: The everybodyfields were a folk and alt-country band from Johnson City, Tennessee, co-founded by Sam Quinn and Jill Andrews, who met at nineteen while working at a summer camp. Their 2004 debut, Halfway There: Electricity and the South, was followed by Plague of Dreams in 2005, the year MerleFest's Chris Austin Songwriting Contest gave them first place. Nothing Is Okay came out on Ramseur Records in 2007, and roots writers heard a move from folk duo to roots rockers. NPR picked Lonely Anywhere as its Song of the Day in February 2008. They played Pickathon that summer.

intro: An Austin offshoot of Grupo Fantasma.
story: Brownout is an Austin Latin-funk band formed in 2003 as a side project by members of Grammy-winning Grupo Fantasma, including guitarist Adrian Quesada and Beto Martinez. Homenaje came out in 2008 and Oozy in 2012. In 2014 they released Brownout Presents Brown Sabbath on Ubiquity Records, with Black Angels singer Alex Maas guesting, and a second volume followed in October 2016. Their 2018 album is Fear of a Brown Planet. They played Pickathon in 2011.

intro: An Ohio trio with seventies-style fuzz and harmony.
story: Buffalo Killers formed in Cincinnati in 2006 after the dissolution of Thee Shams, with brothers Zachary and Andrew Gabbard and drummer Joseph Sebaali. Dan Auerbach of the Black Keys did not know the band existed until he heard their first record, and he recorded their second, Let It Ride, in two weekend sessions at his Akron studio. It came out in July 2008. Dig. Sow. Love. Grow. followed in 2012 and Ohio Grass in 2013 on Alive Naturalsound. They played Pickathon in 2011 with seventies-style fuzz and harmony.

intro: An independent resonator guitarist from the Midwest.
story: Charlie Parr was born in Austin, Minnesota, raised in Hollandale and began his music career in Duluth, which stayed his home base for the next decade. His debut recordings came in 2002, 1922 and Criminals and Sinners, both made in Duluth. Keep Your Hands on the Plow, a set of traditional songs recorded with Duluth musicians including his wife, came out in December 2011. Later albums came on Red House, and Smithsonian Folkways released one in 2021. He played Pickathon in 2011.

story: Tom Heinl is an Oregon singer-songwriter and bingo host known for funny lyrics. His voice has been compared to Kris Kristofferson's and Johnny Cash's. He played Pickathon in 2008.
sets: Fri Aug 1, 6:30 pm, Fir Meadows · Fri Aug 1, 11:30 pm, Heartsong Cabaret

intro: A Montana songwriter from the Reeltime Travelers.
story: Martha Scanlan is a Montana songwriter who came up through the Reeltime Travelers. She has made four solo albums and one collaboration with Portland producer Jon Neufeld, and AllMusic dates The West Was Burning to 2007. The Stuart Brothers, the North Carolina fiddle and banjo twins, toured and recorded with her. She played Pickathon in 2007.

story: Cross-Eyed Rosie is a progressive acoustic band from Portland. They released their own records on their label, Uncle Ostrom Records: Lookin' Up in February 2004 and Adjusted in June 2007. They played Pickathon in 2004.
